primary_reason: The new launch functions do pass their argument verbatim, but the introducing visible-spawn path computes it from provider_key_for_spawn_model(model_override), not from a persisted coordinator runtime/auth key. parent_note: The recorded token-inflation effect is false at intro; only a narrower timing defect holds, which is a new claim.
primary_reason: The claim that tool-call tokens remain in the TPS numerator while their generation time is excluded is false at intro_commit: the same commit gates accumulation on streaming_tps_collect_output, which pause_streaming_tps(false) clears. The fix repairs both timing and final-token collection.
second_check: Confirmed: the intro pauses on ToolStart, which signals tool generation rather than execution.
finding: The introducing diff changes ToolStart to pause the timer, while the agent sends that event on ToolUseStart before generating the arguments. It also stops accumulating tokens, so the record's claimed inflation from continuing to count them is unsupported. The timing defect survives that correction: the fix's test starts timing at ToolStart, asserts the pause at ToolExec, and checks final token collection.

primary_reason: The helper would block on a busy mutex, but the stated reconnect-to-an-existing-busy-Agent trigger is not established at intro_commit. handle_client creates a fresh Agent per connection (src/server/client_lifecycle.rs:123-125,188). handle_resume_session takes that connection Agent by shared reference, locks it before restoring from storage (src/server/client_session.rs:631-643), then inserts that Agent into the sessions map (697-699), rather than adopting the existing busy Agent. On the same connection, resume already waits for the mutex before reaching the added refresh. Therefore the commits do not confirm that this introduction causes the specific busy-reconnect stall claimed.
second_check: Confirmed: awaiting the agent lock on resume or subscribe can block behind the turn.
finding: A reconnect starts with its own Agent, and resume restores the session into that Agent instead of taking the existing turn's Agent from the sessions map. On the same Agent, successful resume already has to await its mutex, and the baseline also takes a snapshot lock in the request path. The fix test holds a mutex directly and verifies the new helper can return, without showing an intro-only busy reconnect stall.

primary_reason: The exact no-docblock trigger is not enabled at intro_commit. inherit_method_docblocks skips children for which needs_docblock_inheritance is false (populator.rs:999); that method tests only INHERITS_DOCS (metadata/function_like.rs:287-288). The scanner returns on a missing docblock (scanner/function_like.rs:286-289) and sets INHERITS_DOCS only for an explicit inheritance tag (330-331). Thus the supplied child with no docblock never reaches the overwrite at this commit.
second_check: Confirmed: the introduced inherited return assignment ignores the child's native type.
finding: The overwrite exists but the introducing populator reaches it only for a child marked INHERITS_DOCS. The scanner returns when the child has no docblock and otherwise sets the flag for explicit inheritance. The fix fixture uses a child with no method docblock, so it cannot exercise this overwrite at the intro.

primary_reason: The claim that the sibling-project example is dropped by strip_prefix is not supported at intro: the unclean path starts with the invoking project prefix and can instead be wrongly retained. The fix test reference_files_across_projects expects no files to check. The underlying failure to clean .. is confirmed.

From frontend, the argument becomes frontend/../backend/app.py relative to the repository, so it passes the frontend prefix check and is wrongly admitted into that project's hook work. primary_reason: The asserted unsigned saturation-to-zero implementation is absent at intro_commit. The actual signed i64 saturating subtraction does not clamp ordinary pre-epoch values to zero, and the unix_secs < 0 guard is reachable. There is a narrower real defect for timestamps less than one second before the epoch because signed division truncates toward zero.
second_check: Confirmed: the saturating subtraction makes the pre-epoch guard unreachable.
finding: The pinned code subtracts signed i64 values and rejects negative whole seconds, so the recorded unsigned saturation and unreachable guard are false. A timestamp one tick before the epoch does truncate toward zero during division, and the fix's test uses exactly that value. The test supports the narrower rounding defect, not the claimed saturation mechanism.

primary_reason: The specified introduction builds a fresh private ThreadPool for every invocation and invokes rayon::spawn within pool.install; it does not run default-thread par-each on the global pool. ls at the same intro also creates its own pool (ls.rs:333,492). The supplied shared-global-pool explanation is not confirmed at this revision.
second_check: Confirmed: ls and streaming par-each share Rayon's global pool.
finding: The introducing revision constructs a private pool for par-each and uses rayon::spawn from inside pool.install, where the current Rayon worker belongs to that private pool. The pinned ls uses the same pattern with its own pool. The fix makes the choice explicit with pool.spawn, and its ls regression does not establish the asserted shared-global-pool topology at intro.

primary_reason: At d5846556, walk_child_exprs explicitly excludes Expr::Const (crates/hir-def/src/expr_store.rs:491-501). The new upvars visitor uses that helper and has no separate const traversal, so it cannot observe the const-local or misclassify it as an upvar for the supplied trigger.
second_check: Confirmed: the introduced closure capture check misclassifies locals inside const blocks.
finding: The new visitor's fallback walks children through ExprStore::walk_child_exprs, which explicitly treats Expr::Const as a leaf. The binding-owner check therefore never sees the const-local reference for the supplied closure. The fix adds a const-block regression during a walker rewrite, but that test does not support the attributed intro behavior.

primary_reason: At intro_commit, stream.rs:239 increments processing before process_batch completes the event at stream.rs:297. For one successfully enqueued and replayed event, dispatch contributes +1/-1 and replay contributes +1/-1, leaving zero rather than usize::MAX. The claimed missing replay increment is contradicted by the code.
second_check: Confirmed: enqueue and replay both decrement processing, producing an atomic wrap.
finding: The intro's dispatch and batching replay each have a balanced increment and decrement for a successfully delivered event. The fix's test calls increment_processed directly for simulated delivery, without the actual intro replay increment. That demonstrates the issue for the later replay accounting contract and cannot reproduce the stated underflow at intro.

primary_reason: The compound claim is only partly confirmed: service accounts are routed as STS, but prepare_auth calls IamSys::is_temp_user (sys.rs:381-389), which calls store.get_user; manager.rs:313-319 searches users and sts_accounts. primary_reason: The claimed Down trap contradicts intro code: current_section_index uses max(topmost, selected_item) (state.rs:304-307), and tree_step advances selected_item to the next section (state.rs:365-367). Moreover ensure_visible returns immediately outside Settings focus (state.rs:778-780), including Categories focus. Right can select section 0 immediately, but subsequent Down is not forced back to it by the stated mechanism.
second_check: Confirmed: the scroll-derived cursor causes broken Down navigation after Right.

The reported stuck mechanism is absent because the section calculation takes the maximum of topmost and selected_item, and tree_step sets selected_item to the next section's first item. The named test checks that Down lands on the first section after expansion, and cannot distinguish a skipped section from the claimed trap.

primary_reason: The intro reserves a separate suggestions layout chunk (src/editor.rs:6346-6364) outside editor_content_area (6424-6433). Buffer cursor placement requires the click inside the split's content rectangle, so falling through the item hit-test does not move it. primary_reason: The claimed wholesale Window::from_workspace replacement is bypassed at intro_commit: move_buffer_membership_to_window inserts the buffer and seeds splits (plugin_commands.rs:1501-1504,1554-1570), so restore_workspace_for sees populated=true (workspace.rs:504-518). primary_reason: At intro_commit, open_terminal still calls create_terminal_buffer_attached, whose unconditional std::fs::write(&backing_file, "") at terminal.rs:137 clears any leftover or colliding transcript after spawn. Only restore uses create_terminal_buffer_detached and loads preserved content (session.rs:558-562). spawn suppresses its writer for nonempty files and never loads their bytes into the fresh TerminalState. Path collisions and erroneous restore inference are real, but the claimed new-terminal scrollback inheritance is not established at this revision; collision can instead erase restored history.
second_check: Confirmed: deferred writer creation and persisted filenames cause a new terminal to inherit old scrollback.
finding: The intro infers restore from a nonempty file and can suppress the fresh PTY's backing writer, but ordinary open_terminal still calls create_terminal_buffer_attached, which truncates the file and does not load its prior bytes. Thus the leftover test does not reproduce inheritance at intro, and the live-restore case's path collision can erase or share a transcript without establishing the claimed inheritance of existing bytes. The fix regression asserts both separate paths and removal of leftover content.

primary_reason: The precise claimed emission is not confirmed: at intro, CommonJs under modern-module resolves to node-commonjs and ESM code imports Node createRequire. The fix changes non-Node targets to plain commonjs and preserves bare require(...); it does not eliminate require because browsers lack it.
